script.base: Book prices NYJ -3.5 in a 39.5 total, implied NYJ 21.5 and MIA 18. Base flow is a low-possession grind: NYJ leads by about a score, Breece Allen (55 carries, 253 rush yards in weeks 4-6) runs the clock, and MIA stays run-lean with Malik Willis rather than a dropback shootout. Pace stays slow.
script.flip1: NYJ gets up by two scores early and MIA abandons Ollie Gordon's carry share (44 carries, 229 yards in weeks 3-5). Allen's rush volume gets safer, Gordon's rush line dies, and Washington/Bell deep air (262 and 239 air yards) stalls because NYJ can blitz at 37% a QB at -0.35 EPA vs blitz. Willis scramble attempts can still rise while chasing.
script.flip2: MIA hangs around or leads on Willis's legs (19 carries, 141 rush yards in the L3 window) and Gordon's 5.2 YPC, so it stays a rock fight near 20-17 instead of a NYJ clock-kill. Both backfields stay full, Garrett Wilson (58.3 rec yds/game) never gets the dropbacks to clear 66, and a shootout stack does not cash.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location splits are the proxy: NYJ allows 7.67 YPA middle (45 att) vs 4.94 left (67 att) and 6.7 right (80 att). MIA allows 9.71 YPA middle (38 att) vs 7.51 left (51 att) and 6.75 right (56 att). Middle is the soft spot for both.
matchup.pressure: NYJ blitz rate 37%. MIA QB EPA/dropback is -0.35 vs blitz (n=50) vs -0.02 with no blitz, so pressure cuts deep WR yards and pushes scrambles plus short throws. MIA blitzes only 27%. NYJ QB EPA is -0.11 vs blitz (n=58) vs +0.13 with no blitz, so Geno is fine on the more common unblitzed look.
matchup.bleeds: NYJ rush defense allows 4.38 YPC and 18 runs of 10+ in 6 games, and 15 passes of 20+ on 209 attempts. MIA is the tighter front at 4.03 YPC and 15 runs of 10+ in 5 games, but bleeds the middle at 9.71 YPA with 13 passes of 20+ on only 149 attempts.
matchup.overlap: The overlap that fits the pressure script is Dulcich, not Washington. Dulcich has 13 targets, 95 air yards (about 7.3 aDOT) and 92 rec yards, into the middle where NYJ allows 7.67 YPA, which is where a blitzed Willis has to throw. Washington (23 targets, 262 air, about 11.4 aDOT, 166 yards) is the downfield option a 37% blitz should suppress. Allen's 18.3-carry role does not meet a weak run front; MIA allows 4.03 YPC. Wilson would overlap MIA's 9.71 middle YPA, but a 39.5 NYJ-leads script may not give him the dropbacks.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Willis ran for 141 yards on 19 carries in the only MIA window in the pack (about 47 a game), and NYJ blitzes 37% against a QB at -0.35 EPA when blitzed, so designed runs plus scrambles should clear 30.5 if that role holds.
edge_players.must_be_true: Willis starts and keeps about 5-7 rush attempts, NYJ's blitz rate stays elevated, and there is no snap cap (none is listed in the pack).
edge_players.kills_it: Jets spy him, Gordon keeps the designed runs, and Willis finishes near 3 carries, or the 7.4 YPC was one long run. A role change in missing week 6 also kills it.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Dulcich is the intermediate outlet (13 targets, 92 yards, 95 air in weeks 3-5, about 31 yards a game), and a 37% Jets blitz against a QB who collapses vs pressure should add checkdowns into the middle, where NYJ allows 7.67 YPA, so 21.5 is light.
edge_players.must_be_true: Dulcich keeps about a 4-target route share, Willis starts and gets the ball out short instead of taking sacks, and NYJ does not erase the middle.
edge_players.kills_it: Willis holds the ball and the -0.35 EPA shows up as sacks rather than completions, or Dulcich is inactive or capped and Washington/Bell take the intermediate looks.

pre_mortem: Monday both lost because the missing week-6 MIA box score already changed the offense, or because the Jets spied Willis: Gordon kept a 14-carry load, Willis had about 4 carries for under 20, and the blitz produced sacks instead of Dulcich catches. A 7.4 YPC and 92 yards on 13 targets do not have to travel, and there is no inactive list to confirm either player is full-go. That counter is real but not stronger than a 47-vs-30.5 rush role plus a middle checkdown into a 7.67 YPA hole, so both stay leans rather than drops.
slip_story: One story: Jets pressure on Willis. Legs that win together are Willis rushyds over 30.5 and Dulcich recyds over 21.5 (scramble plus checkdown). Do not add Washington or Bell overs, which need clean deep dropbacks, do not add a game over onto a 39.5 grind, and do not mix Allen rush over, which needs a separate NYJ-leads clock-control script. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player.
